findings.excerpt: have hcru : c r (Subgroup.inclusion hJX u) = Subgroup.inclusion hJX u := by
findings.problem: `hcommR` and `hub` are the same argument run twice. (1) A normalizer element g (r, resp. x) commutes with `u : J`, so its induced automorphism fixes `inclusion hJX u`; this uses `normalizerMonoidHom_apply_apply_coe`, then rewrites with the commutation hypothesis and `group`. (2) That automorphism equals `MulAut.conj b` (b = `aR r`, resp. `a`), so `b * u * b⁻¹ = u`; the proof then shows `b * u = u * b` with a `calc`. Only the source of g and its commutation fact differ. `hcx_apply` and `hc_apply` (lines 86 and 130) are likewise two copies of one coercion lemma for `normalizerMonoidHom`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a private lemma, stated for any `g : Y` with `hg : g ∈ normalizer X`, any `b : ↥X` with `hb : normalizerMonoidHom X ⟨g, hg⟩ = MulAut.conj b`, and any `u : ↥X` with `(u : Y) * g = g * (u : Y)`. Its conclusion is `b * u = u * b`. Proof sketch: apply `hb` to `u`; use `normalizerMonoidHom_apply_apply_coe` and the commutation to get `conj b u = u`; unfold `MulAut.conj_apply`; finish with the `calc`. The two uses become: `hub u := lemma x hx a ha (inclusion hJX u) (mem_centralizer_singleton_iff.mp (hJc.1 u.2).2)` with `ha` restated through `cx`, and `hcommR r u := lemma (r : Y) (hR r.2) (aR r) (haR' r) (inclusion hJX u) (mem_centralizer_iff.mp (hRJ r.2) u u.2)`. The lemma can be proved once, and the two coercion lemmas collapse into the single unfolding it needs.
findings.benefit: This removes about 30 lines of duplicated reasoning and makes the shared idea explicit: an element of X inducing the same inner automorphism as a centralizing normalizer element centralizes the same set. A fix to either computation then needs to be made only once.

findings.declaration: ggHalfNbrCent_of_centSolv (translating conj a = 1 to a ∈ center / π a = 1)
findings.problem: The local fact `hker : conj.ker = center` is re-applied by hand at five places: `ha3` (116), `map_one'` (210), the `hmem` in `map_mul'` (219), `haK` (243) and `hmemker` (329). Each repeats the same pattern: `rw [← hker, MonoidHom.mem_ker]; change MulAut.conj _ = 1; …`, or `rwa [hker]` and `MonoidHom.mem_ker.mp`. They also repeat the follow-up step `QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff` to move between `a ∈ center`, `π a = 1` and `conj a = 1`. Each use rebuilds the same chain of three equivalences.
findings.proposed_change: After `hker`, add two derived facts and use them throughout. First, `hconj_iff : ∀ b : ↥X, MulAut.conj b = 1 ↔ π b = 1`, proved by `hker`, `MonoidHom.mem_ker` and `QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff`. Second, `hconj_eq : ∀ b c : ↥X, MulAut.conj b = MulAut.conj c → π b = π c`, proved via `b⁻¹ * c` or `map_mul`. Then `ha3`/`hk3` become `(hconj_iff (a^3)).mp (by rw [map_pow, ha, hcx3])`. `φ.map_one'` becomes `(hconj_iff _).mp (by rw [← haR' 1, map_one])`. `φ.map_mul'` becomes `by rw [map_mul]; exact hconj_eq _ _ (by rw [map_mul, ← haR', ← haR', ← haR', map_mul])`. `haK`/`hconj_a` and `hmemker`/`hconj` become `(hconj_iff _).mpr hk1` and `(hconj_iff _).mpr hφr1`. Since this lemma lives inside the proof, no new imports are needed. It could also become a standalone private lemma in the file about `X ⧸ center X`.
findings.benefit: It removes five hand-rolled kernel/center/quotient round trips, so the structure of the homomorphism φ and of the two case branches is easier to read. It also keeps the translation between conjugation, the center and the quotient in one place.
